lesson.topicTitle: Structure and functions in living organisms

specAnchors.text: know the similarities and differences in the structure of plant and animal cells

primer.text: Animal and plant cells share the core eukaryotic kit, but each adds its own extras. This note lists the subcellular structures of an animal cell, the three additions plants make, and the comparison table that turns those lists into exam answers — the similarities AND the differences, side by side.

modules.title: The animal-cell inventory
modules.opening: An animal cell runs on five named structures: a nucleus holding the genetic material, a cell membrane deciding what enters and leaves, mitochondria for aerobic respiration, ribosomes building proteins, and the jelly-like cytoplasm where reactions happen. Some of these are too small for a light microscope and only appear under an electron microscope.
keyPoints: The nucleus contains the cell's genetic material.
The cell membrane controls what enters and leaves the cell.
Mitochondria are the site of aerobic respiration.
Ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis.
Cytoplasm is the jelly-like substance where chemical reactions take place.

low.restatement: Animal cell: nucleus, membrane, mitochondria, ribosomes, cytoplasm — five structures to name and one job each.
low.analogy: Think of a small workshop: the nucleus is the manager's office, the membrane the door policy, mitochondria the generator, ribosomes the assembly bench, cytoplasm the floor everything stands on.
low.examPointer: Pair each structure with its function in one line — 'mitochondria: site of aerobic respiration' is a complete mark.

medium.restatement: Each structure's function follows from its design: the membrane's selective barrier role, the mitochondrion's folded surface for respiration, ribosomes as the protein-assembly site.
medium.analogy: A factory floor plan explains the workflow — where a machine sits tells you what it does.
medium.examPointer: Electron-microscope resolution is a favourite twist: ribosomes and detailed mitochondria need it, so say which microscope an image came from.

modules.title: Plant additions and the comparison table
modules.opening: Plant cells carry everything an animal cell has, plus three structures: a cellulose cell wall that gives shape and protection, a permanent vacuole of cell sap that keeps the cell turgid, and — in leaf and stem tissue — chloroplasts for photosynthesis. The comparison table collects both lists so the shared and unique features sit side by side.
keyPoints: Plant cells add a cellulose cell wall that gives shape and protection.
The permanent vacuole holds cell sap and keeps the cell turgid.
Chloroplasts appear in leaf and stem cells and are the site of photosynthesis.
Nucleus, cytoplasm, membrane, mitochondria and ribosomes sit in BOTH cell types.

low.restatement: Plant = animal kit + cellulose wall + permanent vacuole + (in leaves and stems) chloroplasts.
low.analogy: A plant cell is an animal cell that built a fence (wall), installed a water tank (vacuole) and added solar panels (chloroplasts).
low.examPointer: Learn the table's three plant-only rows — they are the differences examiners ask for.

medium.restatement: The three additions map to three plant problems: support without skeletons (wall), water balance (turgor from the vacuole) and self-feeding (chloroplasts).
medium.analogy: Plants solved the standing-still life with three add-ons: a frame, a reservoir and a solar array.
medium.examPointer: Say 'permanent' vacuole — dropping the word blurs the animal/plant contrast the table draws.

glossary.definition: The watery solution of dissolved substances inside the permanent vacuole.
Describes a plant cell swollen firm because the vacuole presses the cytoplasm against the wall.
The subcellular structure where proteins are synthesised.
